admitted.text: After the bench she seems to decide, in fear, to hide her real self from Pace behind her polished face for good.
admitted.detail_quote: Tenderness was something the face received and passed inward, in amounts she decided.

admitted.text: Her self-possession in public reads as an act that is starting to slip, even in front of her sisters.
admitted.detail_quote: Every other woman she had weighed and released, her attention moving on; this one held her where she stood

admitted.text: Her offer of a threesome reads as cover for a desire for a woman that she can't face directly.
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable

admitted.text: Small private acts of pain read as a way she quietly manages what she feels.
admitted.detail_quote: her thumb had found the rim of her water glass and set the edge of it in under the nail, bearing down.

admitted.text: Randi's refusal of Pace's prepared meal reads as a bodily enactment of deprivation, control, and protest.
admitted.detail_quote: Her bowl on the table where he had set it down, the sauce gone to a skin

admitted.text: With Vee her warmth sometimes seems real rather than staged, like true tenderness.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had just spent something on her, in front of the girls who decided what it was worth.

admitted.text: She seems to want to be the one Vee remembers for life, which is about more than a game.
admitted.detail_quote: Me," Randi said. It came out with Kentucky all the way up in it

admitted.text: She reads as resentful and left out, jealous that Pace has Vee on his own.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend, and you're in no hurry, and I can't think why you would be.

admitted.text: Randi reads as socially brilliant and practiced at making deliberate maneuvers appear warm, accidental, and effortless.
admitted.detail_quote: their shoulders met, Randi giving half a head and enough weight that the accident appeared entirely to happen to her.

admitted.text: He seems truly careful about consent and treats the other person's free choice as the whole point.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: Under that care, he also reads as a planner who steers Vee while keeping his hand hidden.
admitted.detail_quote: So you helped it along a little, and kept quiet, and let it prove in its own time or not at all.

admitted.text: He seems to keep missing Randi's pain, taking her distress for desire.
admitted.detail_quote: It was the want, he thought; she had come for it and got it, more than she could lie still under.

admitted.text: His respect for closed doors seems to come from an old guilt.
admitted.detail_quote: A closed door was hers, not his; you did not open it just because you could hear through it.

admitted.text: He seems loyal to Vee's privacy, even with Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: He kept every piece of it. It was not his to hand across.

admitted.text: His interest in Vee reads as hungry and watchful, a wish to be there as she discovers things about herself.
admitted.detail_quote: He wanted to hear her. He wanted to be in the room.

admitted.text: He seems generous and attentive almost to the point of devotion, remembering things Vee had already let go of.
admitted.detail_quote: He'd said *that sounds like a beautiful dress,* taken another cherry, and the talk moved on.

admitted.text: Pace reads as courtly without being bloodless, his restraint making his appetite more visible rather than less.
admitted.detail_quote: that he wanted her, that he was choosing the dress and the doing-it-right over the easy yes she was all but handing him

admitted.text: Pace seems to confuse helping Vee discover desire with earning the right to conceal the game that brought him to her.
admitted.detail_quote: So you helped it along a little, and kept quiet

admitted.text: She reads as starved, emotionally as much as physically, and only now letting herself be fed.
admitted.detail_quote: It kept going down and down into something that had been empty a lot longer than since noon.

admitted.text: Her mother's voice of shame seems tangled up with her arousal, so the two feed each other.
admitted.detail_quote: she could not find the seam between the heat and the shame because there was no seam

admitted.text: She seems dazzled by Randi and longs to be chosen by her.
admitted.detail_quote: She had stood outside this exact joke. Now she was walking under it with Randi

admitted.text: Vee reads as ravenous for sustained attention because being chosen seems to make ordinary experiences feel like admission into a brighter life.
admitted.detail_quote: She had not been keeping the words. She had been keeping the feeling

admitted.text: She seems to desire Randi without ever letting herself look at that desire.
admitted.detail_quote: the want had nowhere to put itself except here, this, with her, and it sat there in Vee's chest, warm, unexamined, glad.

admitted.text: She seems quick to explain away Randi's kisses so she doesn't have to know what they mean.
admitted.detail_quote: She had it explained away almost before her mouth was her own again.

admitted.text: She has started keeping the most intimate parts of her life from Cassie.
admitted.detail_quote: She believed it the way you believe the thing that lets you keep what you want to keep.

admitted.text: By the end she reads as growing into a bold pride in her own body.
admitted.detail_quote: she stood in the middle of the light and let them look. It just felt like what she was for.

admitted.text: Vee reads as discovering that choosing openly can make her feel more fully herself than merely being wanted.
admitted.detail_quote: I wasn't talked into it. I did it because I wanted to and I did it on purpose.

admitted.text: Vee seems to trust Pace because his restraint repeatedly leaves her room to advance rather than making her defend a boundary.
admitted.detail_quote: He wasn't going to take it any further than she had. Whatever came next was hers too.

admitted.text: Vee reads as constantly negotiating money and status, determined not to let Randi purchase her place even when independence costs her.
admitted.detail_quote: She did the small arithmetic, the kind that ended in Thursday, and found that Thursday would survive it.

admitted.text: She reads as fiercely loyal and protective of Vee in quiet ways.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie never asked — asking was for people who wanted the sad version to get bigger.

admitted.text: She seems to notice something off about Randi that Vee misses.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie was watching Randi thumb at her phone, her own pencil stopped in her hand.

admitted.text: She seems to feel herself being left behind and hides the hurt.
admitted.detail_quote: by the time Cassie's eyes came back to Vee's, whatever had been in them was folded away.

admitted.text: Cassie reads as noticing more of Vee's omissions and changes than she forces into the open.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie listened with her chin on her knees and did not pull at the seam.

admitted.text: Under her warmth she reads as a watchful president quietly building a case against Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: said Brooke, like she was filing it.

admitted.text: Brooke reads as a polished enforcer whose warmth makes scrutiny and rank harder to challenge.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke's voice was always warm. She had a voice the way other people had a perfume.

admitted.text: She reads as a gently skeptical voice about new love.
admitted.detail_quote: Everybody's different at the start.

admitted.text: Kayla reads as exuberantly invested in turning Vee's uncertainty into a romantic event.
admitted.detail_quote: We're doing hair Saturday. I'm coming to your room. This is happening.

admitted.text: The bench hidden inside a table: a hidden purpose and appetite that will come back.
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: Thin apple slices: a woman who rations her own wants.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: The lock and the deadbolt: Randi shutting herself away from being known.
admitted.detail_quote: the size of a key turning in a lock.

admitted.text: The burning maple: a desire that has changed color before anything around it has decided to change.
admitted.detail_quote: a single tree burning orange in a field of things that had not yet decided to change

admitted.text: Euler's two parts at right angles: the hidden design of three people becoming one thing.
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: The pool: Vee's lost sense of belonging in her body before it became a problem.
admitted.detail_quote: Nobody up there could see her. Nobody down here wanted anything.

admitted.text: Packing out the cherry pits: Pace's care, and perhaps a habit of leaving no evidence.
admitted.detail_quote: She had it and he hadn't made her small to give it to her.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: Pace giving up his own comfort for her, which she then holds onto.
admitted.detail_quote: It was soft, and it was warm — not warm from a body

admitted.text: Error-correcting codes: messages repeated so they survive noise, a hint of the hidden plan's built-in redundancy.
admitted.detail_quote: Say it more than once so the noise can't kill it.

admitted.text: The burgundy silk: being seen and matched as she really is, not as she imagined.
admitted.detail_quote: Everything she'd ever worn had been cut for no one in particular. This one had been cut to the actual shape of her, and to no one else's.

admitted.text: Randi's white-gold band: one fixed, unexplained bond or private weight.
admitted.detail_quote: the one fixed thing in a wardrobe that changed itself daily.

admitted.text: The folded panties given in trade: Vee offering her wanting as a gift instead of a shame.
admitted.detail_quote: She kissed him, briefly, and held the folded panties out toward him.

admitted.text: The covered, uneaten bowl: Randi's refused nourishment and Pace's baffled care.
admitted.detail_quote: He covered the bowl with a plate and put it in the refrigerator, for her, and turned the light off over the stove.

admitted.text: the hip-high slit: visibility that opens and closes with Vee's own movement, making exposure something she can actively choose
admitted.detail_quote: The slit fell open on her bare leg, calf to hip, and this time nothing crossed it.

admitted.text: When Vee learns that Randi and Pace chose her together, how will she take it?
admitted.detail_quote: He had no name for the game yet, only the live private charge of something he imagined they could make together.

admitted.text: Will Randi ever come back out from behind the face she put back on in the mirror?
admitted.detail_quote: He could have the face. The face was very good.

admitted.text: What happened with Daphne, and what did it cost Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: it had cost him more than he had known, then, that anything could cost.

admitted.text: How much does Cassie already understand about the danger or loss she sensed when Randi first drew Vee away?
admitted.detail_quote: something passed over her face, brief, that Vee would not have been able to name and did not try to.

admitted.text: Will Vee admit to herself that she wants Randi?
admitted.detail_quote: She had it explained away almost before her mouth was her own again.

admitted.text: Where do Pace's scars and marks come from?
admitted.detail_quote: a scar, large, high on the inside of his thigh.

admitted.text: Why did the mention of Pace's parents make him close down, and what history is he withholding?
admitted.detail_quote: Something crossed him at parents — a small closing, there and gone, a door easing shut two rooms away.

admitted.text: What is really wrong with Randi, beyond jealousy over Friday?
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend, and you're in no hurry, and I can't think why you would be.

admitted.text: How will Vee respond when she learns the real purpose of the bedroom table whose design she currently mistakes for an early failure?
admitted.detail_quote: It doesn't look like him. It must have been the first thing he ever designed himself.

admitted.text: Will the induction give Vee the unapologetic public arrival she now daydreams about?
admitted.detail_quote: In the daydream she didn't fold her arms or find the wall; she stood in the middle of the light and let them look.

admitted.text: How will Vee understand her freely chosen desires once she knows that Pace and Randi concealed both their relationship and their plan?
admitted.detail_quote: So you helped it along a little, and kept quiet, and let it prove in its own time or not at all.
